sent_to_model:
I'm replying to a discussion asking whether physical punishment as a child affected you afterward. I want to say yes, although I still struggle to call what happened abuse because my parents made me believe I deserved it. Can you help me describe how Dad's punishments escalated and the ear injury and operations? I want to explain the fear, loneliness and lack of affection, what still affects me, and why I'm determined not to treat my own children that way. Seeing a therapist after I left for college helped me finally tell someone. Please include that too. Please also say that I don't know whether any of this made me a better or worse person.

- Dad stopped the attacks after first ear operation.
- At college, began therapy; telling someone helped.
- One of Dad's beatings ruptured an eardrum, leaving about one-third missing; doctors waited a year before surgical repair.
- Father weighed roughly 250 pounds; writer around 120 at about twelve.
- Later operation needed; approximately a year after Dad moved out.
- Physical attacks had become daily after school.
- Father moved out about a year after the ear incident.
- First surgery: tympanoplasty; summer spent recovering in recliner.
- Parents said punishments were deserved; writer accepted blame.
- Initial punishments around age six involved severe pinching on ears, back, legs and arms.
- Face slaps later replaced pinches; sometimes repeated.
- Guest sleeping in writer's room smashed a ringing alarm; father blamed writer and punched them in a dark bedroom.
- With braces in early ninth grade, repeated punches left mouth sores and indentations.
- Doctors found ear damage inconsistent with soccer; accepted writer's account despite recognizing it was likely false.
- Small amounts of teenage backtalk could prompt punches.
- School bruises went unexplained from embarrassment; others seemed to assume clumsiness.
- Poor grades or complaints from Mom and sister could trigger punishment.
- Once sister complained after writer entered her room to ask about her day.
- Still flinches at sudden upward hand movements.
- No way to recover the childhood affection missed.
- As a young child, assumed other homes were similar.
- Cannot tell whether the experience improved or worsened personal character.
- Childhood felt unsafe; tiny mistakes could provoke anger.
- Could not talk to parents or confide in others.
- Suspects guilt may explain Dad's departure; his actual reasons unknown.
- Determined not to repeat the treatment with future children.

(About me: person reflecting on childhood. Length: it should come to roughly 800-2,000 words.)

must_cover: Explain the hesitation to call the punishments abuse and describe their escalation.
Describe the ear injury and the operations it required.
Convey childhood fear, loneliness and missing affection, along with effects that persist.
Explain the determination to parent differently and how therapy after leaving for college helped.
Convey uncertainty about whether these experiences made the writer a better or worse person.
